key_insight: A magnetic-field-induced hydrodynamic potential modifies ion distributions in flowing electrolytes, producing a Hall potential that is nearly linear in flow velocity and magnetic field strength but largely independent of salt concentration.
engineering_relevance: The framework can inform magnetic control and interpretation of ion transport in microfluidic and electrochemical systems.
method: Couple steady-state Navier–Stokes, Nernst–Planck, and Poisson equations for unidirectional electrolyte flow.
Derive ion distributions incorporating electrostatic and hydrodynamic potentials, then analyze Poiseuille flow and counterion-only conditions.
Examine two-dimensional entrance transients to distinguish rapid electrical adjustment from slower salt redistribution.
evidence_signal: Analytical results and entrance-region analysis support the predicted Hall response and separation of electrical and salt-transport length scales; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Applicability beyond dilute electrolytes and steady, unidirectional flow requires further validation.
paper_title: Theory of magneto-electrokinetics in unidirectional electrolyte flow: Hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect
